newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Workers at Romania aircraft plant threaten unrest.
newsitem.headline: Workers at Romania aircraft plant threaten unrest.

text.p: Romanian workers at the Craiova Avioane SA aircraft maker, where production was halted by the war in ex-Yugoslavia, on Wednesday threatened to start protests to demand relaunched production and job security.

"Our workers are scared and desperate. We have no other choice but go ahead with plans for protests next month," Ion Ionescu, vice-president of CA trade union, said from Craiova, near the Bulgarian border.
The union wants executives to ensure orders and come up with a coherent project to relaunch production at the plant and guarantee jobs for its 2,700 workers, down from 4,700 five years ago.

The Craiova plant was built in the 1970s with an initial investment of $100 million, part of a joint Romanian-Yugoslav project to build 200 IAR 93-Orao sub-sonic jet fighter-bombers for the air forces of the two neighbouring Balkan states.
But trade sanctions imposed by the United Nations on former Yugoslavia over its role in the Bosnian war brought the plant, 250 km (150 miles) west of Bucharest, to a virtual standstill.
